ten.surface_rating.label: Surface-adjusted player rating (Elo/serve-return)
ten.surface_rating.mechanism: A latent player strength on the match's surface summarises opponent-adjusted results; surface speed and bounce make skills non-transferable across hard, clay and grass.
ten.surface_rating.rationale: Match outcome is the cleanest function of relative strength on the actual surface; overall Elo blends surfaces and mis-prices specialists, while pure surface Elo is noisy because there are few matches on grass. Subtle: a blend (surface Elo weighted with overall Elo by sample size) usually beats either, and rating freshness after injury or layoff matters.
ten.surface_rating.measurement: Fit overall Elo and surface-specific Elo (K higher for new players, lower with tour experience, bo5 weight), blend with weight w(n_surface) = n/(n+k) (k ~ 30-50 matches); use tour-level plus Challenger/ITF results for lower-ranked players; time-decay for layoffs; use only matches before the decision date.

ten.serve_return.label: Serve/return point-win probabilities by surface
ten.serve_return.mechanism: Points won on serve and return are the primitive inputs of tennis: the serve-return pair determines hold and break probabilities and every derived market (sets, games, totals).
ten.serve_return.rationale: Match probability is a deterministic function of serve-point and return-point win probabilities (Markov hierarchy), so these capture style more precisely than a scalar rating, particularly for totals and set-score markets. Subtle: raw averages mix opponents of different quality; the pair must be opponent-adjusted and surface-specific.
ten.serve_return.measurement: Per player and surface: spw = points won on serve / serve points, rpw = points won on return / return points from match stats; adjusted via ridge on logit with opponent effects (spw_ij = mu_surface + serve_i - return_j); shrink with n/(n+k) (k ~ 1000 service points); recency half-life ~ 12 months.

ten.h2h_style.label: Head-to-head and style matchup
ten.h2h_style.mechanism: Particular styles (lefty serve, big server vs weak returner, heavy topspin vs flat hitters) create matchup residuals beyond overall rating.
ten.h2h_style.rationale: Head-to-head records capture matchup residuals but are tiny samples and mostly reflect rating gaps; stylistic features (handedness, serve profile, return aggressiveness) are better. Subtle: raw H2H overstated by selection (they meet often because both are high-ranked, on specific surfaces) and should be shrunk very heavily.
ten.h2h_style.measurement: Residual of observed result over rating-implied probability, aggregated over H2H meetings with shrinkage n/(n+10); alternative: style-pair regression using handedness, serve speed, rally length profile.

ten.form.label: Recent form and match-load
ten.form.mechanism: Recent results reveal updating information about fitness, confidence and equipment/coaching changes not yet fully in the rating.
ten.form.rationale: Form beyond rating is weak (ratings already update), but form dips can signal hidden injury, and wins in prior rounds signal match sharpness. Subtle: easy draws inflate 'form'; the adjusted measure should compare results to rating expectation (surprise) not raw wins.
ten.form.measurement: Rolling mean of (actual result minus rating-implied win prob) over last 10 matches (weights decay), tour-level only, plus count of matches in last 30 days.

ten.fitness.label: Fitness/injury/withdrawal and in-match retirement risk
ten.fitness.mechanism: Physical condition (injury, illness, fatigue) lowers performance and raises the probability of retirement or walkover.
ten.fitness.rationale: Injury news is discontinuous and often leaks late (practice absence, medical timeouts, withdrawals the day of the match). The market partially prices it but the settlement consequences (void, retirement rules) matter as much as performance. Subtle: unobservable injuries dominate; recent retirements and layoffs are the best observable proxies.
ten.fitness.measurement: Features: retirement/walkover in last 12 months, days since last match, previous-round match length, medical-timeout flags from live score feeds; calibrate retirement hazard from historical rates (see ten.retirement_base_rate).

ten.fatigue.label: Fatigue (match length, back-to-back days, travel)
ten.fatigue.mechanism: Accumulated court time and short recovery reduce movement and serve quality and raise injury hazard, particularly in best-of-five events.
ten.fatigue.rationale: Previous-round match duration, sets played and days of rest are known pregame; effects are modest and heterogeneous by age and fitness. Subtle: weak competition lowers fatigue; extreme duration (five-setters, night finishes) has the strongest effect; effect interacts with format and heat.
ten.fatigue.measurement: Minutes and sets played over last 7 and 14 days, days since last match, late-finishing flag, travel zone change; regress rating-residual on these with player-level shrinkage.

ten.format.label: Match format (best-of-3/5, tiebreak, ad scoring)
ten.format.mechanism: Best-of-five amplifies the favourite's edge (more points played so skill variance averages out) and changes fatigue dynamics; tiebreak and final-set rules change game counts.
ten.format.rationale: A fixed per-point edge translates to a larger match-win probability in bo5 than bo3, and total games/sets markets differ by format; final-set tiebreak rules (advantage set vs tiebreak at 6-6 / 12-12 / 10-point) change length distributions. Subtle: format differs by tournament and round and by tour (WTA is bo3 almost everywhere), so a lookup table of rules by event-year is required.
ten.format.measurement: Lookup of events by year: sets to win, final-set rule, tiebreak points, no-ad; feed into the Markov match model; check interaction with fatigue and format-specific ratings.

ten.hold_break.label: Hold/break probabilities and game-level Markov model
ten.hold_break.mechanism: Hold and break probabilities, derived from point-win probabilities via the game-level Markov chain, drive set scores, game counts and totals.
ten.hold_break.rationale: Service hold ~ nonlinear amplification of serve-point probability, so small differences in point probabilities create large hold differences; this is the main engine of games, sets and spreads. Subtle: points are not exactly iid (pressure, serve alternation), and uncertainty in spw should be propagated into the match distribution.
ten.hold_break.measurement: Compute p_hold = f(spw_i vs rpw_j adjusted) via closed-form game formula; p_break = 1 - p_hold of opponent; set/match probabilities by dynamic programming; propagate uncertainty by sampling spw from posterior.

ten.set_dist.label: Set/score distribution and correlations
ten.set_dist.mechanism: The joint distribution of set scores follows from hold/break probabilities with within-match dependence (form fluctuations, momentum), affecting exact-set, total games and set spreads.
ten.set_dist.rationale: Independence across sets underestimates the frequency of lopsided matches (3-0 sweeps) and decisive sets; between-set correlation arises from day-level form and player-specific variance. Subtle: dependence parameters are hard to estimate; ignoring them mis-prices tail scores.
ten.set_dist.measurement: Fit a Markov model with a latent match-form shock to spw (random effect) and calibrate on historical distribution of set scores and match lengths by tour and surface.

ten.aces_df.label: Aces/double-fault rates, serve speed, court speed
ten.aces_df.mechanism: Aces and double faults are driven by serve speed and placement, the opponent's return, court speed and conditions, and by the number of service games played.
ten.aces_df.rationale: Aces per service game is a stable player trait; the expected count is that rate times service games (depends on match length) with opponent return adjustment and surface/ball/altitude factors. Subtle: count depends on how the settlement source counts, on retirements/shortened matches, and on first-serve percentage variance.
ten.aces_df.measurement: Ace rate = aces per service point, opponent-adjusted via a negative-binomial/Poisson GLM with server and returner effects and surface; expected service points from match-length model; overdispersion parameter estimated by player.

ten.draw.label: Draw/bracket structure and round-by-round simulation
ten.draw.mechanism: A tournament win requires surviving a specific path of opponents; the bracket, seeds and potential matchups determine round-by-round probabilities.

ten.market_odds.label: Closing bookmaker odds
ten.market_odds.mechanism: Sharp closing odds aggregate ratings, injury information and sharp money, so they are the benchmark any tennis model must clear.

ten.tiebreak.label: Tiebreak win rate and hold-under-pressure
ten.tiebreak.mechanism: Tiebreak outcomes are close to coin flips tilted by serve strength; the probability a set reaches 6-6 depends on both players' hold probabilities.

ten.break_points.label: Break points created/converted/saved
ten.break_points.mechanism: Break-point creation reflects return quality; conversion/saved rates mix skill and luck and mostly regress to serve/return levels.

ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return.label: Opponent-adjusted serve and return components

free_sources: ATP and WTA public sites (atptour.com, wtatennis.com: draws, scores, stats, rankings, race, order of play)

ten.team_event_structure.label: Team-event rubber structure and lineup selection
ten.team_event_structure.mechanism: Team competitions (Davis Cup, United Cup, Laver Cup) are decided by multiple rubbers with singles/doubles, captain decisions and varied formats.
ten.team_event_structure.rationale: Team outcomes require lineup probabilities, surface choice by the host, rubber format (best-of-three, deciding doubles) and fatigue; individual ratings do not transfer one-for-one because of captain choices and home advantage. Subtle: nominations are announced shortly before ties; format changes across editions.
ten.team_event_structure.measurement: Probability of each lineup from nominations and captain history; rubber win probabilities from individual models; simulate tie outcomes; adjust for home/surface.

ten.points_defense_rolling.label: Rolling ranking points, points to defend and race state
ten.points_defense_rolling.mechanism: Season ranking and qualification outcomes depend on points already earned, points dropping off from the previous year and the calendar of remaining events.
ten.points_defense_rolling.rationale: Season-ranking and qualification markets are determined by the 52-week rolling points mechanics (ranking) or season race points; a player's expected change is predicted by results and by the points they defend. Subtle: mandatory events, zero-pointers and injured players distort simple projections.
ten.points_defense_rolling.measurement: Points timeline from official rankings and last year's results; expected points per event from the draw simulation; simulate remaining season rankings with participation probabilities.

ten.joint_event_correlation.label: Joint outcomes across co-listed tennis events
ten.joint_event_correlation.mechanism: Combo markets require the joint probability of several tournament outcomes, which share participation, form and injury risk across events.
ten.joint_event_correlation.rationale: Multiplying independent outcome probabilities misprices combos: a top player's injury affects all events they enter and also removes chance for rivals; mutually exclusive structures (same player cannot win both if events are simultaneous) must be handled. Subtle: dependence is mostly through participation and health.
ten.joint_event_correlation.measurement: Joint simulation across events with a shared player-health state; compute joint probabilities and compare with product of marginals.
free_sources: ATP and WTA public sites (atptour.com, wtatennis.com: draws, scores, stats, rankings, race, order of play)

ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.label: Probability a set reaches 6-6
ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.mechanism: A tiebreak happens only when both players hold serve through 6-6, so its probability depends on both hold probabilities and their match-form variance.
ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.rationale: Tiebreak-occurs markets are essentially functions of the product of two hold probabilities and the Markov chain probability of reaching 6-6; pairs of big servers on fast courts are strongly favoured, while return-oriented matchups on clay rarely reach 6-6. Subtle: probability is sensitive to small errors in hold, and the match-level number of sets matters for 'at least one'.
ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.measurement: Compute P(6-6 in a set) from the game-level Markov chain with adjusted hold; combine across expected sets (including bo5) with within-match dependence; calibrate by event.
free_sources: Jeff Sackmann tennis_atp / tennis_wta match CSVs (github.com/JeffSackmann: atp_matches_YYYY.csv, wta_matches_YYYY.csv, rankings, players)

ten.server_game_state.label: Server identity and game-level state for in-play games
ten.server_game_state.mechanism: Within a game, the server is a strong favourite and the score state (break point, deuce) changes win probabilities sharply.
ten.server_game_state.rationale: In-play game-winner prices depend on who serves, the point score and the server's current spw; the only pregame knowledge is the model of how spw evolves. Subtle: data feed delays and the first-server selection affect which player serves odd/even games.
ten.server_game_state.measurement: Closed-form game win probability by score and spw; update spw with posterior in-match; include first-server advantage per set.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/tennis/<tour>/scoreboard)

ten.score_feed_latency.label: Score-feed latency and settlement source timing
ten.score_feed_latency.mechanism: Live prices depend on the freshness of the score feed; stale scores create stale quotes and adverse selection.
ten.score_feed_latency.rationale: In point-level markets the observed lag between the courtside score and public feeds is large relative to price changes; trading on stale information is the dominant risk or edge. Subtle: this is infrastructure rather than prediction.
ten.score_feed_latency.measurement: Measure delay between event time (if available) and feed timestamp; track price lag after score changes.

ten.market_margin_bias.label: De-vig method and favourite-longshot bias in tennis lines
ten.market_margin_bias.mechanism: Closing-line margin and favourite-longshot bias distort implied probabilities; the right de-vig method changes the baseline probabilities for heavy favourites.
ten.market_margin_bias.rationale: In two-way markets the longshot side tends to be overpriced; when comparing Kalshi prices to book odds the correction matters for lopsided matches. Subtle: bias differs by tour and round and must be estimated on out-of-sample data.
ten.market_margin_bias.measurement: Calibration of closing implied probabilities vs outcomes by probability bucket on tennis-data.co.uk history; fit power/Shin; use to correct comparison.

ten.suspension_postponement_risk.label: Rain suspension and postponement risk
ten.suspension_postponement_risk.mechanism: Rain or curfew can suspend, postpone or move a match to another day or court, with fatigue and settlement consequences.
ten.suspension_postponement_risk.rationale: Suspended matches may resume the next day with altered conditions and rest, and markets may close or settle differently; roofed courts change risk. Subtle: forecast precipitation uncertainty is high.
ten.suspension_postponement_risk.measurement: Probability of rain at start and during match window; roof/indoor flag; historical rain-delay rate by venue; map rules_text on suspension.

ATP and WTA public sites (atptour.com, wtatennis.com: draws, scores, stats, rankings, race, order of play)

ten.surface_calendar.label: Surface-season transition effects
ten.surface_calendar.mechanism: The switch between surfaces (hard to clay to grass) in the calendar creates adaptation lags that are surface-specific and player-specific.
ten.surface_calendar.rationale: Players in the first events of a new surface season are less sharp, and ratings built on previous-surface results over-credit specialists; the effect is largest for the clay-to-grass change with only a few events. Subtle: knowledge of players' adaptation history is partial.
ten.surface_calendar.measurement: Number of matches played on the current surface in the last 60 days; days since surface switch; interaction with surface similarity.
free_sources: Jeff Sackmann tennis_atp / tennis_wta match CSVs (github.com/JeffSackmann: atp_matches_YYYY.csv, wta_matches_YYYY.csv, rankings, players)

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series
m.quote_history.mechanism: Prices aggregate dispersed information; the path of the quote (and its drift toward kickoff) reveals when informed flow arrives and how stale an early quote is.
m.quote_history.rationale: A resting Kalshi quote hours before first serve is partly stale: team news, injury and line moves at sharp books arrive in bursts, and Kalshi liquidity is thin so quotes can lag. The quote path also defines the realistic entry price (not a mid that was never tradable). Subtle: last-trade can be far from the executable bid/ask, and closing-quote efficiency is a benchmark rather than a given.
m.quote_history.measurement: Snapshot bid/ask/mid/last at fixed horizons (T-24h, T-6h, T-1h, T-10m, close); compute spread, time since last trade, and signed drift vs the sharp-book de-vigged price at the same timestamp. Never use post-start quotes for pregame features.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Executable size at each price level, not the mid, determines how much edge can be captured and what slippage costs.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: A model edge of two cents is worthless if depth at the touch is a handful of contracts; wide spreads on long-shot rungs mean the quoted probability is mostly spread. Depth also signals whether a market maker is active (tight, refreshed quotes) or the book is abandoned (stale quotes that will be picked off when news lands).
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Record top-5 level price/size per side, cumulative depth within 1/2/5 cents of mid, spread in cents and as fraction of price; compute expected fill price for a target size.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Traded volume and open interest proxy how much information and capital has been committed, hence how trustworthy the price is.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-volume rungs are usually closer to sharp consensus; thin rungs deviate and can be mispriced but are also costly to trade. Volume spikes near the news window reveal when informed trading happens. Subtle: volume is cumulative by market and cannot be compared across markets with different contract caps without normalising.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Per market: cumulative volume, OI, volume in the last hour before close, volume rank within the family; log-scale features and ratios to family median.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Games/sets/spread ladders must be monotone and mutually consistent with the match-winner market; kinks expose mispriced rungs and the implied game-differential distribution.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Each rung is priced separately by different participants, so the implied pmf (differences between adjacent cumulative prices) can go negative or be implausibly lumpy. Fitting a smooth parametric distribution across rungs and trading the residual is a market-structure edge that does not depend on a view about the teams. Subtle: push rules and integer vs half-point lines change which rung differences are legitimate.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Collect all rungs of an event at one timestamp; check monotonicity of cumulative prices; fit a constrained distribution (game-differential from a hold/break Markov model) by least squares on mid prices and record per-rung residuals and implied pmf.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: Settlement is the realised label; the exact settled value and timestamp (not the box-score) is what pays.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Labels must be taken from Kalshi's recorded settlement, not re-derived from a stats site: edge cases (extra time, abandoned matches, retirements, source corrections after the fact) can make the settled value differ from the intuitive result. It is never a pregame feature but is the ground truth for backtests and for measuring how often wording edge cases occur.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join each market to its settled result/value and settlement time; flag markets whose settled value disagrees with an independently computed result as wording/void cases.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); settled market fields (result, settlement_value, settlement_ts)

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording
m.rules_text.mechanism: Wording fixes the event: retirement/walkover handling, minimum completion for set/game/ace markets, rain suspension carry-over, source of record and tie rules.
m.rules_text.rationale: Retirement and walkover handling is the dominant settlement risk in tennis: some markets void or refund when a player retires before completion, others settle on the final state; ace/game totals may need a minimum number of games played. Mis-reading these rules turns a model edge into a loss. Subtle: wording differs by market type and can change across seasons, so it must be parsed per market and versioned.
m.rules_text.measurement: Store rules text with a version hash at each fetch; parse into flags (regulation_only, includes_ET, includes_pens, void_if_abandoned, void_if_retired, min_games_required, source_of_record) and use them as hard filters/feature switches.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); market rules_primary / rules_secondary fields

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook/exchange reference prices
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp external prices are an information-rich prior; a Kalshi price that disagrees with the de-vigged sharp close either carries a stale quote or genuine information.
m.external_lines.rationale: The sharp closing line is the best-known single predictor in most sports markets, so any model must clear it, and its de-vigging method matters (proportional vs Shin vs power) especially for 3-way markets and long-shots. Subtle: timestamps must be matched; using a closing price against an earlier Kalshi quote overstates edge (look-ahead), and free historical files only give open/close snapshots.
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each external quote (Shin for 3-way/long-shot-heavy sets, power for two-way), timestamp-match to the Kalshi quote, compute the Kalshi minus sharp probability difference and its sign persistence.
free_sources: tennis-data.co.uk odds spreadsheets (Pinnacle/Bet365/Max/Avg closing odds)
Betfair Exchange historical data (data.betfair.com basic plan)

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realised edge nonlinearly in price (larger relative drag near 50c and for small expected edges), so the net-of-fee probability threshold differs by rung.
m.fees.rationale: A model edge below the fee-plus-spread hurdle is not tradable; the hurdle depends on price level and on maker vs taker. Fee rules change over time so a historical backtest must apply the schedule in force on the trade date. It does not predict the outcome but determines which model edges are monetisable.
m.fees.measurement: Implement fee(price, size, role, date) from the schedule; compute net edge = model_p minus price minus fee/contract minus half-spread; evaluate decisions on net edge.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule PDF / help center (kalshi.com/fee-schedule)

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: The lifecycle (open, close before start, halts, postponement, early settlement) controls when information can still be traded on and which markets get voided or re-opened.
m.lifecycle.rationale: Tennis start times are only estimates (order of play, rain), so a market can sit open for hours or close on a different court time than the model assumed; suspensions and walkovers create halts and voids.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Log status transitions with timestamps; compute minutes between last tradable quote and event start; flag postponements, delays >30 min, halts and re-opens.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); market status/open_time/close_time/expiration fields

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Calibration by rung exposes systematic mispricing at specific strikes (e.g. favourite-longshot bias, popular round numbers) independent of any team model.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Ladders attract round-number and narrative bias: some rungs settle YES more often than priced, others less. The frequency table is a prior and a calibration check for the model, not a causal input; it needs enough settled history per family/strike and a shrinkage rule to avoid chasing noise.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: For each family and strike bucket: realised YES rate minus average de-vigged pre-close price, with Wilson intervals; shrink toward zero by n/(n+k).
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks) settled history (result by strike per family)

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time)
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Trade prints with taker side show where aggressive flow went, how fast the price moves after trades (impact) and what fills were realistically achievable.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Order-flow imbalance before the news window can foreshadow lineup/injury information; trade size distribution separates informed from retail flow; post-trade price reversion measures adverse selection. Subtle: public tape lacks participant identity, so flow signals are noisy and must be validated out of sample.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Compute signed volume imbalance (taker side), VWAP vs mid, price impact over the next 1/5/30 minutes, trade count and size quantiles per market per hour.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks) /markets/trades endpoint

ten.ace_count_distribution.label: Ace and double-fault count distribution
ten.ace_count_distribution.mechanism: Counts over service points are over-dispersed and depend on surface and the opponent's return.
ten.ace_count_distribution.rationale: Ace ladder markets need the whole count distribution; per-point ace probability by surface and opponent, number of service points (set length) and within-match dependence set it. Subtle: tiebreaks add service points.
ten.ace_count_distribution.measurement: Negative-binomial or beta-binomial over expected service points with per-point ace probability from opponent-adjusted serve and return data by surface.
free_sources: Jeff Sackmann tennis_atp/tennis_wta match stats (w_ace, w_df, w_svpt)
tennis-data.co.uk results

ten.ranking_points_simulation.label: Ranking-points simulation over the tournament calendar
ten.ranking_points_simulation.mechanism: Rank and major-count markets are tails of points accumulated over a calendar of tournaments.
ten.ranking_points_simulation.rationale: A player's rank depends on points defended and available at each event; the calendar structure (points dropping off after 52 weeks) is deterministic, outcomes are not. Subtle: injuries and withdrawals dominate the lower tail.
ten.ranking_points_simulation.measurement: Simulate remaining tournaments from own rating, entry probability and draw difficulty; track points added and dropped; output rank and major-count distributions.
free_sources: ATP/WTA rankings history (Sackmann rankings files)
Official calendars

ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.label: Cross-surface rating covariance
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.mechanism: Joint posterior of a player's hard, clay and grass ratings, which determines how much a title on one surface predicts another.
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.rationale: Treating each surface rating as independent makes consecutive-title joint probabilities too low; a pooled rating treats them as identical and makes them too high.
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.measurement: Fit a hierarchical Elo model with a player-level vector (hard, clay, grass) and a covariance matrix Sigma estimated across players (typical correlation 0.5-0.8); report posterior covariance for each pair of surfaces for the player; use it in the joint simulation to draw correlated surface-specific strengths. As-of: before the first leg.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (surface column)
Tennis Abstract surface Elo

ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.label: Event-to-event carryover after a title
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.mechanism: Empirical probability of winning the next event given a title at the previous one, by calendar gap and surface change.
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.rationale: The combination probability needs P(leg 2 | leg 1), which depends on the load of leg 1, the gap and the surface transition; the historical frequency of consecutive major titles provides a calibration target.
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.measurement: From history of pairs of consecutive majors compute P(title at event 2 | title at event 1) for the same player by gap days (<=21, 22-42, >42) and surface change (clay to grass, grass to hard), as a ratio to the product of marginal probabilities; shrink the ratio toward the model-implied ratio with weight n/(n+8). As-of: before the first leg.
free_sources: Wikipedia major champions lists
Sackmann CSV

ten.health_persistence_between_events.label: Health persistence between consecutive events
ten.health_persistence_between_events.mechanism: Probability a player is fit for event j+1 given fit at event j and a deep run, estimated from consecutive entries.
ten.health_persistence_between_events.rationale: Shared health links legs for one player; persistence differs by age and prior load.
ten.health_persistence_between_events.measurement: From historical consecutive event pairs for top-50 players compute P(start event j+1 | started event j), by age bin, prior-run depth (rounds, minutes), and gap days; logistic with shrinkage n/(n+30). Use in the joint simulation as a player-level state. As-of: before the first leg.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (entries via results)
Wikipedia draw pages

ten.leg_resolution_state.label: Leg resolution state and conditional collapse
ten.leg_resolution_state.mechanism: State of each leg (open, won, lost) and the conditional probability of the remaining legs.
ten.leg_resolution_state.rationale: A combination whose first leg has resolved Yes is just the remaining legs' joint probability; a lost leg makes it zero; the leg structure determines how the conditional probability collapses as legs resolve.
ten.leg_resolution_state.measurement: Track per contract each leg status with timestamp; compute P(combo | resolved legs) from the joint simulation conditional on resolved legs; flag combinations whose legs have mutually exclusive outcomes; as-of: official result time.
free_sources: Official tournament results

ten.set_first_server_sequence.label: First server in each set (serve-order sequence)
ten.set_first_server_sequence.mechanism: Which player serves first in each set is a deterministic function of the start of the match and game parity, and first-serve shifts set-win probability.
ten.set_first_server_sequence.rationale: The existing catalog models hold and break but does not carry set-by-set serve order; for evenly matched big servers a coin-toss-driven first-serve advantage shifts the 2-0 versus 2-1 split. A tiebreak resets the rotation, so conditional on a tiebreak in set 1 the order in set 2 differs from the no-tiebreak case.
ten.set_first_server_sequence.measurement: Serve order after toss: set 1 first server S1 (from toss; unknown pre-match, treat as 0.5/0.5 until announced). Set k first server = opponent of the player who served the last game of set k-1 unless set k-1 ended with a tiebreak, in which case the player who received first in that tiebreak serves first. Compute P(set win | first server) by running the game-level chain for each of the 12-game sequences. Output per-set first-server probabilities conditional on tiebreak history. As-of: toss result (about 15 minutes before play) for the live case; pre-match treat unknown.
free_sources: Sackmann point-by-point files (serve sequence)
ATP/WTA live scores

ten.straight_set_share_curve.label: Empirical straight-set share by pre-match edge
ten.straight_set_share_curve.mechanism: Probability that the winner takes the match without dropping a set as a function of pair edge, tour and format.
ten.straight_set_share_curve.rationale: This is a calibration curve (not a market price): it tells how much of the match-win probability mass historically converts to the sweep versus decider scorelines, which a purely i.i.d. model gets wrong.
ten.straight_set_share_curve.measurement: From Sackmann match scores for the past ten years, compute for bins of pre-match Elo-implied win probability (in 5-point bins, split by tour, best_of, surface) the share of matches won 2-0/3-0 and the share reaching a decider; shrink bin shares toward a logistic fit with weight n/(n+40); report P(2-0 | A wins) and P(deciding set). As-of: ratings available before each historical match.
free_sources: Sackmann CSVs (score strings)

ten.retirement_timing_profile.label: Retirement timing distribution by set
ten.retirement_timing_profile.mechanism: When a retirement happens decides which exact-score rungs are already settled.
ten.retirement_timing_profile.rationale: A retirement after set 1 resolves different rungs than one in set 3; the existing retirement base rate does not carry timing.
ten.retirement_timing_profile.measurement: From Sackmann score strings containing RET, parse the number of completed sets and the set-score at retirement; estimate P(retire in set k | retirement) by tour, round, best_of and by which player was trailing; shrink toward tour pooled with n/(n+30). Output: P(retirement before completing set 1/2/3), P(retiring player trailing).
free_sources: Sackmann CSV score field with RET

ten.in_match_spw_posterior.label: In-match running serve-point posterior
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.mechanism: The server's spw during the match is a posterior combining the pregame pair prior with the points played so far.
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.rationale: The existing catalog lists the live point stream but not the update rule; the trade-off between prior weight and observed points is the central modelling choice.
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.measurement: Beta-binomial: spw_post = (k*spw_prior + wins_so_far)/(k + points_served_so_far) with k fit by maximising held-out game log-likelihood on historical point sequences (start with k=60 points, range 30-120); allow a separate k for first-serve points and second-serve points; add an exponential forgetting factor of 0.98 per point when a medical signal fires. Updated after every point, timestamped to the feed clock.
free_sources: Sackmann slam point-by-point for calibration of k
live feed in production

ten.ball_change_cycle.label: Ball age and ball-change schedule
ten.ball_change_cycle.mechanism: New balls favour the server and change the ratio of hold probability across the first games after a ball change.
ten.ball_change_cycle.rationale: Slam and tour rules change balls after seven games and then every nine games; a game right after a ball change is played with livelier balls. The magnitude is small and event-specific, so the sign and size must be estimated, not assumed.
ten.ball_change_cycle.measurement: Per-event ball-change register first: record for each event whether new balls come after 7 then every 9 games, after 9 then every 11, or on another schedule, and whether the count includes the warm-up (event-dependent; the register is a required dataset). Then games_since_ball_change = (total games played - first_change_game) mod interval for the event's schedule, with a flag for the first game on new balls; estimate delta_hold by regression of hold outcome on that flag controlling for server, surface and event using point-by-point data; report in spw points. Where the event schedule is not in the register the input is missing, not imputed.
free_sources: ATP and WTA rulebooks
Sackmann point-by-point (game sequences)

ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.label: Deuce-court versus ad-court serve and return asymmetry
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.mechanism: A player's serve and return win rates differ between the deuce and ad sides, and break points are mostly played on the ad side in this lead-in.
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.rationale: The point score determines which side the point is played from, so game state and side are tied; lefties and right-handers differ systematically.
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.measurement: From charted points, estimate spw_deuce and spw_ad per server and the returner's rpw on each side with shrinkage n/(n+80); expected game win probability computed with side-specific spw along the score path (e.g. 30-40 and 40-40 on the ad side). Sparse for non-charted matches.
free_sources: Jeff Sackmann MatchChartingProject (limited coverage)
Sportradar point data (paid)

ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.label: Shot-clock and violation state
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.mechanism: The serve clock and warnings change second-serve timing and can produce a lost first serve or point penalty inside a game.
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.rationale: Time violations take away a first serve or award a point in limited cases; in tight finals the umpire's discretion varies and affects the point score directly.
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.measurement: Count of time violations and code violations per match from official or broadcast logs; estimate violation hazard per player and chair umpire (shrunk n/(n+20)); for a live game include a binary flag if a warning has been issued. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for structured violation logs.
free_sources: Broadcast and official match reports (manual coding)
Sportradar events (unverified)

ten.player_speed_slope.label: Player-specific court-speed response slope
ten.player_speed_slope.mechanism: A player's strength is a function of continuous court pace, not just a hard/clay/grass label.
ten.player_speed_slope.rationale: Overall Elo blends surfaces and surface Elo is a three-way categorical split. Court speed varies a lot inside 'hard' (Indian Wells slow, Paris indoor fast). Players differ in their sensitivity: big servers gain on fast courts, baseliners lose.
ten.player_speed_slope.measurement: For each player fit Elo_i(c)=Elo_i0 + beta_i*(CPI_c - mean CPI) with CPI from event ace-rate/hold-rate index over the previous three editions (hold% over tour average, with time-decay half-life one year). Estimate beta_i by ridge regression on that player's last ~120 tour matches using only matches completed before the as-of date; prior beta mean from serve profile (ace rate, height) with ridge penalty lambda ~ 20 matches. Output the speed-adjusted Elo for the match event. Leave-player-out rule: the event CPI used for player i is recomputed excluding every match involving player i (and the same player's other events), so beta_i is not fit against an index containing its own serve and return results; each remaining match's hold and ace residual is first adjusted for the two players' own tour-surface baselines to reduce field-composition contamination (field composition is still not fully removable, see mw_speed_index_source).
free_sources: Sackmann CSV aggregates (hold%, ace rate by tourney_name)
Tennis Abstract surface splits

ten.level_transfer_offset.label: Challenger/ITF to tour rating offset
ten.level_transfer_offset.mechanism: Players move between Challenger/ITF and tour level, and ratings fitted on different pools are not on the same scale.
ten.level_transfer_offset.rationale: Kalshi lists Challenger matches (KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH) where one player may have 80% of recent matches at ITF level and the other on tour; a pooled Elo with a single scale overstates the lower-level player.
ten.level_transfer_offset.measurement: Estimate level offsets by fitting Elo on all levels with a level-dummy per player pool: offset_L estimated from players who played at both levels in the previous 24 months (mean rating change across a level crossing, shrunk with n/(n+25)). Apply offset_L to each player's rating before computing the gap. Recompute weekly with data available at the as-of timestamp.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (tour, Challenger and ITF rows)
ITF world tennis rankings public pages

ten.doubles_pair_strength.label: Doubles pair strength and partnership continuity
ten.doubles_pair_strength.mechanism: A doubles winner is a pair-level outcome: net play, serve-plus-one patterns and chemistry matter beyond two individual singles ratings.
ten.doubles_pair_strength.rationale: KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPDOUBLES and KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES settle pairs that often formed days earlier. Singles rating is a weak proxy: doubles specialists with weak singles records dominate.
ten.doubles_pair_strength.measurement: Pair rating = 0.6*mean(doubles Elo of each player, shrunk with n/(n+15) toward 1500) + 0.25*pair Elo (zero if <5 shared matches) + 0.15*mean singles Elo scaled by 0.3. Add penalty term for first-time partnership (-20 Elo if 0 prior matches, linearly vanishing at 10). Use only matches before as-of timestamp; format modifiers for match tiebreak and no-ad. The weights 0.6/0.25/0.15, the n/(n+15) shrinkage, the -20 Elo debut penalty and the 10-match fade are initial placeholders to be fitted by out-of-sample log loss on doubles history, not calibrated values; the doubles rule set (no-ad, match tiebreak) is coded per event by ten.format (unresolved mw_doubles_format).
free_sources: Sackmann doubles CSVs (atp_matches_doubles)
ATP doubles rankings public pages

ten.exhibition_format_effort.label: Exhibition format and effort proxy
ten.exhibition_format_effort.mechanism: Exhibitions use shortened formats and non-binding stakes, so the usual ability-to-result mapping is distorted.
ten.exhibition_format_effort.rationale: KXTENNISEXHIBITION is a winner market whose format may be short sets, a match tiebreak or time limit; player effort is discretionary and favourites may coast.
ten.exhibition_format_effort.measurement: Binary flags for event class (exhibition, invitational, team exhibition) plus format descriptors (sets to win, games per set, match-tiebreak, no-ad) coded from the event announcement; shrink the Elo-implied win probability toward 50% by a factor estimated from historical exhibition results (target shrink 0.6-0.8, to be fit when data exist). As-of: announcement date.
free_sources: ATP/WTA and promoter announcements
Wikipedia exhibition pages

ten.walkover_slot_hazard.label: Walkover and late-withdrawal hazard by slot
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.mechanism: Pre-start walkovers and lucky-loser swaps remove a match from the payoff set or change the participants.
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.rationale: The sampled rule sends non-occurrence to a fair price, so the exposure is to price drift in the final hours before a withdrawal becomes public, not to a final loss. Hazard varies by round, event tier and days since last match.
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.measurement: Empirical day-level hazard h(round, tier, days_since_last_match, last_match_minutes>150, age>=33) = share of scheduled matches ending in a W/O score (withdrawal after the draw is made, including lucky-loser replaced slots) in the Sackmann-style score field; logistic regression with shrinkage toward round-level means (n/(n+30)). Sackmann score strings carry NO withdrawal timestamp, so this historical estimate is a single per-match rate; horizon-specific P(WO) at T-48h/T-12h/T-2h must be built from own-captured order-of-play and entry-list snapshots going forward (see unresolved mw_wo_vintage) and is not backfillable. As-of timestamp: order-of-play publication time.
free_sources: Sackmann-style score field W/O rows (access unverified, see mw_sackmann_access)
Own capture of ATP/WTA daily order-of-play pages (forward only)

ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.label: Compatriot collision matrix by round
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.mechanism: The probability that two players of the same nation meet before a given stage and so cannot both advance.
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.rationale: The union probability of a nationality contract falls below the independent union by the collision term; the term depends on draw positions and the probability both survive to the meeting round.
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.measurement: For each pair of compatriots in the draw find the earliest round where they can meet (from bracket positions), compute P(both reach that round) times P(they meet | both reach) = 1 (if bracket position forces), and the loss to union = P(meet) * min(p_i, p_j conditional). Use simulation output from the draw; before the draw, average over draw randomness conditional on seeding. As-of: draw publication.
free_sources: ATP/WTA draw pages
Wikipedia draws

ten.nationality_designation_status.label: Nationality designation and neutral-status register
ten.nationality_designation_status.mechanism: Which players the league designates as the nation's, including neutral designations and allegiance switches.
ten.nationality_designation_status.rationale: The contract defers to the governing league's designation; players with neutral status or dual nationality can be inside or outside the nation's set, and that changes the union.
ten.nationality_designation_status.measurement: Register per player: designated nation as shown on the tournament draw sheet and ATP/WTA player profile (the contract defers to the 'Governing League'; use the draw-sheet flag at draw publication as the primary value and the ATP/WTA profile as the check), passport nation, neutral-athlete flag, date of last change; flag players whose designation differs across sources and treat them as a binary uncertain-membership case. No source exists for the probability that a designation changes before settlement, so it is carried as a scenario flag, not an estimated hazard (see nt_designation_source). As-of: draw publication.
free_sources: ATP/WTA player profiles
Wikipedia player pages

ten.host_surface_selection.label: Host surface and court speed selection in team events
ten.host_surface_selection.mechanism: The host nation picks the surface and sometimes the court speed to favour its players in team ties.
ten.host_surface_selection.rationale: The rubber probabilities depend on the surface and pace; a host that picks a slow clay court changes which players are favoured relative to neutral ratings.
ten.host_surface_selection.measurement: From tie announcements record the surface, indoor/outdoor and pace descriptor; compute each nominated player's pace-adjusted rating (Elo + speed slope * pace) and the change in tie win probability against neutral-surface ratings. As-of: surface announcement (typically weeks before the tie). SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for pace data.
free_sources: ITF Davis Cup and BJK Cup announcements
event pages

ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.label: Team tie lineup distribution
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.mechanism: The set of nominated singles players and doubles pair and the captain's likely choices.
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.rationale: A tie result is determined by the lineup, which is announced late and depends on nominations, fitness and captain history.
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.measurement: Probability distribution over lineups: P(player nominated) from nomination lists (usually 4-5 players); P(starts singles 1/2) from captain history and rankings; doubles pair from past ties and partnership record; rubber win probabilities from pace-adjusted ratings; simulate the tie (best of three or five rubbers). As-of: nomination list publication.
free_sources: ITF nominations
official team pages
press

ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.label: Group tie-break order and rubber results
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.mechanism: The order of tie-breakers (ties, rubbers, sets, games) and the current group state decide advancement in close groups.
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.rationale: Advancement in a group of three or four can come down to sets and games ratios, so the margin of wins matters, not only the win.
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Encode event rules (ordered tie-break criteria), current group table, remaining ties; simulate remaining ties with rubber distributions and compute advancement; flag cases where games ratio decides (probability > 5%). As-of: after each tie.
free_sources: ITF rulebooks
official group tables

ten.home_slam_depth_prior.label: Home-nation depth prior at home majors
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.mechanism: Historical distribution of the number of home-nation players reaching each round at their own major.
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.rationale: A calibration prior for union contracts (such as 1+ Americans in the final) that checks the union model against history.
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.measurement: For each nation and major, compute frequency of at least one home player reaching R16, QF, SF, F over the last 15 editions with decay half-life 6 years; blend with the path-model value using an initial weight of 0.3 that is a placeholder to be fitted on held-out editions (not calibrated); report by tour. As-of: before event. Because a historical home-progress frequency partly re-encodes the strength the model already captures, use it only as an out-of-sample calibration check on the union probability, not as an extra driver inside the model.
free_sources: Wikipedia Slam draw pages
Sackmann CSV (nationality column)

ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.label: Service-points exposure by match scenario
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.mechanism: The player's service points are a mixture over match scenarios and depend on points per service game.
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing match-length input is an expectation; the ace distribution depends on the full exposure distribution and its correlation with the ace rate (a player serving well wins quickly and serves fewer points).
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.measurement: For each player compute N = sum over scenarios s (straight-set win/loss, 3-set, 4-set, 5-set, with and without tiebreaks) of P(s) * (service games_s * E[points per game | spw, rpw] + tiebreak serve points); E[points per game] from the point-score Markov chain (about 5.3 at spw 0.65). Keep the scenario weights from the set-count distribution and from hold probabilities. As-of: before match. Add a retirement scenario: with probability P(ret) from ten.retirement_base_rate (by tour, round, best_of, pre-match fitness flag) the match stops at game g drawn from the retirement-timing distribution, so N is truncated to the service points served before g; the count at retirement is then compared with each rung under ten.retirement_settlement_rules.
free_sources: Sackmann serve counts and scores

ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.label: Serve direction mix versus returner weakness
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.mechanism: Ace probability depends on direction (wide, body, T) and side and on the returner's weaker wing.
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.rationale: The pair interaction is where most of the variance in ace rate sits; direction frequencies are player-specific and known.
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.measurement: From charted points compute the server's share of wide/body/T by side and the ace rate by direction, and the returner's unreturned share by direction; expected ace probability = sum over direction of share_server * (ace rate by direction adjusted by returner weakness); shrink with n/(n+80). Coverage is limited to charted matches.
free_sources: Match Charting Project
Sportradar point data (paid)

ten.line_calling_regime.label: Line-calling regime and foot-fault enforcement
ten.line_calling_regime.mechanism: Electronic line calling versus human line judges and foot-fault enforcement change which serves count as aces or faults.
ten.line_calling_regime.rationale: Systematic differences in service-box calls can shift ace and fault counts by small amounts; regime differs by event and year.
ten.line_calling_regime.measurement: Event-year flags for electronic line calling and for line judges; estimate the regime effect on ace rate by regressing ace per service point on the regime flag with player and surface effects; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the event list by year.
free_sources: ATP/WTA announcements and rulebooks
Wikipedia event pages

ten.second_serve_risk_policy.label: Second-serve risk policy
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.mechanism: The double-fault rate depends on how aggressively a player hits the second serve, which varies with the returner and the score.
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.rationale: Double-fault counts are not just noise: players who hit big second serves against aggressive returners fault more.
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.measurement: Per player, estimate P(DF | second serve) as a function of returner aggression (share of second serves attacked), score pressure (break point flag), and age; shrink with n/(n+60); output expected DF rate against this returner. As-of: day before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann serve counts (df and second serve counts)
Match Charting Project

ten.first_serve_speed_trend.label: First-serve speed trend within and across matches
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.mechanism: Serve speed in the current event and its decay over the match predict ace rate.
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.rationale: Pre-event speed averages mask injuries and form; in-event speed from earlier rounds is a direct indicator of the current serve state.
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.measurement: Per player compute mean first-serve speed in the last two matches and in the previous 10 matches (if published), z-score vs career; expected ace rate adjusted by elasticity beta estimated per player; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for availability of serve-speed data outside the majors.
free_sources: Event statistics pages (not verified)
Hawk-Eye or Sportradar speed data (paid)

ten.layoff_survival_curve.label: Layoff survival curve by injury class
ten.layoff_survival_curve.mechanism: Time-to-return distribution after an injury layoff, conditional on injury class and public statements.
ten.layoff_survival_curve.rationale: The catalog has a generic comeback input but a time-to-return contract needs a survival curve with censoring; the key is the probability of returning before a fixed date given days already missed.
ten.layoff_survival_curve.measurement: Kaplan-Meier estimate of return time from the last match date, by injury class (wrist/elbow, knee, back, foot, illness, surgery vs no surgery), from historical layoffs of at least 30 days; condition on days already elapsed (residual-life curve); shrink class curves to pooled with n/(n+20); output P(return by date T | state at as-of). Public statements enter as a shift of the hazard (statement types coded).
free_sources: Wikipedia player season pages
ATP/WTA player activity pages
press coverage

ten.eligible_event_calendar.label: Eligible event calendar inside the window
ten.eligible_event_calendar.mechanism: The number and type of events a player can enter before the deadline set the number of chances to return or participate.
ten.eligible_event_calendar.rationale: A return before a date is a union across entry opportunities with different entry and incentive probabilities.
ten.eligible_event_calendar.measurement: For each player and window, list events with entry deadline after as-of, surface, category and points; P(entry) = P(eligible) * P(commit); P(return by T)=1-prod(1-P(enter_e)*P(start_e|enter)). Entry deadlines from tour calendars. As-of: before each deadline. Event scope: include ATP Tour main-draw events and the majors (the only scope the sampled note confirms); Challenger, team-event and exhibition entries are carried as a separate flagged set and excluded from P(return) until rp_atp_match_scope is clarified.
free_sources: ATP/WTA official calendar
tournament entry deadline pages

ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.label: Protected ranking, wildcard and cutoff pathway
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.mechanism: Whether a returning player can enter depends on ranking cutoff, protected-ranking use and wildcard probability.
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.rationale: A healthy but low-ranked returnee needs a protected ranking or a wildcard; both are discrete and time-limited.
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.measurement: Binary flags and values: current ranking, protected ranking value and expiry, use count, entry cutoff of each event (last direct acceptance in recent editions), wildcard history of the tournament; P(eligible)=1 if rank<=cutoff else P(wildcard or protected use). As-of: entry list publication.
free_sources: ATP/WTA rulebooks
entry lists on official sites

ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.label: Withdrawal hazard timeline from entry deadline to first ball
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.mechanism: Probability of withdrawal at each interval: before the draw, after the draw before order of play, before the first match.
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.rationale: The hazard is time-varying and clusters near the start; intervals carry different information, which determines when a market should move.
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.measurement: Estimate hazard in intervals (entry to draw, draw to OOP, OOP to first ball) from historical entry lists, draws and results by event category, rank band, age, and days since last match; logistic with shrinkage n/(n+30); as-of: vintage of the entry list snapshot (needs own capture).
free_sources: Entry list and draw archives (Wikipedia, official sites)
own captured snapshots

ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.label: Retirement announcement hazard by age and rank
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.mechanism: Annual and within-year hazard of announcing retirement given age, career length, ranking trend and injuries.
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.rationale: The retirement contract is a low-probability tail event that depends on structured career variables and on announcement habits.
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.measurement: From historical career-end records for players with careers of at least eight years: hazard by age bin (30-31, 32-33, ..., 38+), rank band, injury layoff flag, prior announcements; discrete-time logistic; shrink to pooled with n/(n+25); output the probability of an announcement effective by the deadline. As-of: before the decision date. Avoid survivorship: the at-risk set must include every player with an eight-plus-year career in each age bin whether or not he later announced (active players censored at the as-of date), not only players found on retirement lists; the announcement date itself is taken from the dated statement, not the final match.
free_sources: Wikipedia retirement lists
ATP/WTA player bios

ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.label: Remaining-points arithmetic to the snapshot date
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.mechanism: Maximum and minimum achievable ranking points by the settlement date for each contender, given drop-offs and remaining events. The same race arithmetic also settles Finals-qualification contracts (cutoff at the 8th place, alternates).
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.rationale: In early November the rank is almost mechanically bounded; probability of overtaking is zero unless the gap is less than the maximum swing, and nonzero only through a small set of events.
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.measurement: For each player compute P_end = P_now - drop(t..T) + sum over remaining events of earned points; maximum earned by event structure (for example Finals: 200 per round-robin win, 400 semifinal, 500 final, 1500 undefeated; Masters 1000 etc.); minimum from not playing; compute the probability of rank 1 (or top 5) by simulation constrained by these bounds; update after each event. As-of: after each Monday publication. Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL; title only): qualifier count is eight singles places, the cutoff is the 8th-place Race to the Finals total at the qualification date, a withdrawn qualifier is replaced by the next alternate in race order, and the probability of qualifying is the simulated probability of finishing in the top eight after applying participation hazards; special exemptions (for example the treatment of Grand Slam winners outside the top eight) and doubles-team qualification are not modelled and are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (sr_finals_qual_contracts).
free_sources: ATP/WTA ranking and race pages
tournament points tables from rulebooks

ten.major_participation_hazard.label: Probability of entering each remaining major
ten.major_participation_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters and starts a major) for each of the four majors of 2027, conditional on age, injury state and recent history.
ten.major_participation_hazard.rationale: A major title probability multiplies a participation probability by P(win | play); a veteran or an injured player can have participation well below 1.
ten.major_participation_hazard.measurement: Per player and major, estimate P(start) = 1 - hazard(withdraw before first round), using historical Slam participation by age bin (>=35: lower), injury layoff flag (days since last match>60) and entry list status; logistic with shrinkage n/(n+20). As-of: before each draw.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (Slam rows)
Wikipedia Slam draws

ten.bo5_rating_premium.label: Best-of-five rating premium
ten.bo5_rating_premium.mechanism: Some players outperform their best-of-three rating in best-of-five Slam matches because of endurance or consistency.
ten.bo5_rating_premium.rationale: Men's majors are best-of-five; ratings fitted mainly on best-of-three matches can mis-rank contenders for a major.
ten.bo5_rating_premium.measurement: Elo residual in bo5 matches versus bo3 matches per player (last 60 bo5 matches, half-life 3 years), shrunk toward the tour mean difference with n/(n+25); output bo5 premium in Elo points added to the gap in Slam matches. As-of: before the event.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (best_of column)

ten.major_winner_concentration.label: Concentration of recent major winners
ten.major_winner_concentration.mechanism: Share of recent majors won by the top one or two players, a measure of how top-heavy the title distribution is.
ten.major_winner_concentration.rationale: The title probability distribution across players should have a concentration level consistent with history; ratings alone may not reproduce the top-heavy shares.
ten.major_winner_concentration.measurement: Compute the Herfindahl index and top-2 share over the last 12 majors with weights decaying by edition; compare to the model-implied concentration and shrink player probabilities toward the history-implied shares with an initial weight of 0.3 that is a placeholder to be fitted on held-out majors (not calibrated); update after each major. As-of: after each major. It is a calibration check on model-implied concentration, not a driver multiplied into player probabilities.
free_sources: Wikipedia and official Slam results

ten.career_major_count_state.label: Career major-count state
ten.career_major_count_state.mechanism: The state variable for cumulative contracts: the player's singles major count and any titles won since the contract was issued.
ten.career_major_count_state.rationale: The 25th-major contract is path-dependent on the count; a title already won shifts the target, and doubles titles are excluded.
ten.career_major_count_state.measurement: Count of singles major titles per player with each date; compare to the contract's target at the as-of date; flag if the count differs from contract assumption. As-of: after each major final.
free_sources: Official tournament results
Wikipedia player pages

ten.ranking_publication_calendar.label: Ranking publication calendar and snapshot rule
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.mechanism: Which published list applies at the stated settlement clock depends on the publication calendar.
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.rationale: The settlement uses the most recently published list, so a Thursday year-end resolves to the last Monday list; the lists at weeks without events may be identical to the prior one.
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.measurement: Table of publication dates for ATP and WTA by year; for a settlement time T, the applicable list is the latest publication <= T; check history of publications in late December in prior years (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).
free_sources: ATP/WTA ranking pages
Sackmann rankings files

ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.label: Hold-gap implied expected games margin
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.mechanism: Expected games differential over a full 12-game window is 12 times the difference of the two hold probabilities, a quantity with its own measurement noise.
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.rationale: The model reduces to a simple relationship between hold gap and margin that is easy to estimate and check; the catalog has hold and break but not the margin as a first-class variable.
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.measurement: For each set compute E[D_set] = E[N_set] * (h_A - h_B), where E[N_set] is the expected number of games actually played in the set (about 9.7-10.4 for tour sets, counting a 7-6 set as 13 games; take it from a DP over set scores given h_A and h_B), not a fixed 12: each game moves the margin by the hold gap on average, but a set stops at 6-x, 7-5 or 7-6. Worked check by DP: h_A=0.85, h_B=0.75 gives E[N]=10.1 and E[D_set] about 1.03, whereas 12*(h_A-h_B)=1.20 overstates it by about 17 percent. Better still compute the set margin PMF by the DP directly and average over who serves first. h comes from opponent-adjusted spw via the closed-form hold formula (spw 0.65 gives hold 0.83); sum over expected sets with weights from match-length probabilities; report mean and standard deviation of the margin with spw sampled from its posterior (SD of spw about 0.015). Base: match CSV w_/l_ serve points with a 12-month half-life, as of the day before (source access unverified, see sp_sackmann_access).
free_sources: Sackmann CSV w_svpt, w_1stWon, w_2ndWon, l_ columns

ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.label: Calibrated game-margin probability mass function
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.mechanism: The empirical distribution of match games differential by pre-match edge, format and tour, with tiebreak-induced discreteness.
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.rationale: Smooth normal approximations miss the 1-game masses created by tiebreaks and the 5-6 game tails created by bagels; a calibrated PMF corrects both and is not a market price.
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.measurement: Build the empirical PMF of D (games A minus games B) from Sackmann score strings (retirements excluded and modelled separately), by bin of pre-match Elo-implied win probability (5-point bins), tour, best_of, surface; smooth with a kernel over adjacent bins and shrink to a parametric fit with weight n/(n+50). Report P(D>k) for half-integer k. As-of: ratings before each historical match.
free_sources: Sackmann match score strings

ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.label: Margin given win conversion curve
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.mechanism: The probability that a match winner also has a games margin above a threshold, as a function of pair edge and format.
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.rationale: Spread settlement mixes winner and margin; the share of wins that are close (negative or small margins) rises as the gap shrinks and in best-of-five, and matters more than the mean margin at the strike.
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.measurement: From Sackmann scores compute for each edge bin P(D>k | winner) and P(D<0 | winner) by format; fit a logistic in edge and format; shrink to pooled values with n/(n+60). Combine with the winner probability: P(D>1.5)=P(win)*P(D>1.5|win)+P(lose)*P(D>1.5|lose). The edge bins use the market-free P(win) from the match_winner model (surface- and pace-adjusted Elo variant, stated in the dataset), never a price-implied probability.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings

ten.game_serial_dependence.label: Serial dependence of game results within and across sets
ten.game_serial_dependence.mechanism: The chance a player holds depends on whether he was just broken and on set-state pressure.
ten.game_serial_dependence.rationale: Independent game results understate the clustering of breaks; the thickness of the margin tail relies on this serial effect.
ten.game_serial_dependence.measurement: From game sequences, estimate P(hold | prior game was a break against this server) minus P(hold | otherwise) controlling for server and set-level state; include an indicator for serving to stay in the set; estimate pooled effect and player heterogeneity with shrinkage n/(n+60).
free_sources: Sackmann point-by-point game sequences

ten.retirement_margin_state.label: Games margin at retirement
ten.retirement_margin_state.mechanism: If the match is truncated by retirement, the games differential at that moment determines whether the spread rung can be settled.
ten.retirement_margin_state.rationale: The margin at retirement is usually favourable to the non-retiring player and is smaller than a typical completed-match margin; the spread settlement depends on it.
ten.retirement_margin_state.measurement: From Sackmann score strings with RET, extract games for each player at retirement; estimate the distribution of D at retirement by tour and by which player retired; shrink pooled with n/(n+30). Report P(D>1.5 | retirement).
free_sources: Sackmann CSV score with RET

ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.label: Set-count distribution by edge and format
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.mechanism: The probability mass over 2/3 sets (bo3) or 3/4/5 sets (bo5) as a function of pair edge, surface and tour.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.rationale: Total sets and set spread contracts are direct functions of this distribution; 'any set' is its straight-set complement. The existing catalog lists match length in games but not the set-count distribution.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.measurement: Empirical P(N sets) from Sackmann scores by Elo-implied win-probability bin (5-point bins), best_of, surface, tour; smooth by monotone logistic in edge; add 1.5-point shrinkage per bin with weight n/(n+40); expose P(decider), P(winner dropped a set), P(straight sets) per format. As-of: ratings before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann scores

ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.label: Hold-rate uncertainty propagation (Jensen correction)
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.mechanism: Because P(6-6) is convex in hold, uncertainty about hold raises expected tiebreak probability.
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.rationale: Plugging point-estimate holds into the tiebreak formula understates the probability by a few points: averaging 0.80 and 0.90 gives 0.30 while the probability at the mean hold 0.85 is 0.28.
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.measurement: Draw spw_A, spw_B from Beta posteriors with effective n = serve points over the last 12 months (half-life 12 months), add day shock sd 0.02 on spw, convert to holds, compute set 6-6 probability by DP for each draw, average over 2,000 draws; report E[p66] and E[p66]-p66(E[h]). As-of: stats before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann serve counts

ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.label: Tiebreak and sweep base rates by event and format
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.mechanism: Empirical frequency of at least one tiebreak per match, and of straight-set wins, by tournament-edition and format.
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.rationale: Event-level conditions (indoor courts, altitude) produce persistent tiebreak rates that exceed what player stats imply; the base rate is a prior to be updated by the pair.
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.measurement: For each tournament, compute the share of matches with at least one tiebreak and the share won without dropping a set over the last three editions, weighted with half-life 18 months and shrunk to the tour-level rate with n/(n+60); provide split by round and best_of. As-of: before the event.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings (tiebreak shown in parentheses)

ten.player_set_drop_propensity.label: Player set-drop propensity beyond rating
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.mechanism: Some players win more matches in straight sets than their rating implies, others drop sets habitually.
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.rationale: The sweep probability depends on the pattern of set loss, not only on win probability; style and consistency produce heterogeneity.
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.measurement: Per player, residual = share of wins in straight sets minus the model expectation given opponent rating; average over the last 60 wins with half-life 12 months and shrink to 0 with n/(n+25); test split-sample persistence before use; include format and round.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings

ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.label: Joint table of tiebreak occurrence and straight-set win
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.mechanism: Tiebreak occurrence and sweeps are not independent because big-serving pairs produce many 7-6 7-6 straight-set wins.
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.rationale: If the two contracts are listed together, their dependence is relevant for combined pricing and for checking that marginals are consistent.
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.measurement: From Sackmann scores compute the 2x2 table (any tiebreak, straight-set win) by bin of mean hold and hold gap with smoothing; shrink to independence with weight n/(n+80) and report odds ratio by bin.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings

ten.tournament_set_drop_path.label: Tournament-level set-drop path probabilities
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.mechanism: The probability that a player wins a whole tournament without dropping a set is a product across rounds of per-match straight-set probabilities.
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.rationale: If KXATPSETSWEEP means a tournament-level sweep (title unclear), the contract is a path product with the seven or more match-level straight-set probabilities, and correlated with the title probability itself.
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.measurement: For each round r with expected opponent distribution from draw simulation, P(straight sets in r)=P(win)*P(sweep|win) from ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge; multiply across rounds with a correlation adjustment (shared form shock) estimated from historical title runs; output P(title without dropping a set) and compare to P(title). Requires draw and opponent distributions as-of.
free_sources: Sackmann scores for historical runs

ten.set_number_calibration.label: Set-index and previous-set calibration offsets
ten.set_number_calibration.mechanism: Win probability for a given edge differs by set number and by the previous set's result.
ten.set_number_calibration.rationale: The match model implies a single set-win probability but empirical frequencies show set-index effects (first set cautious, deciders fatigue and tiebreak formats). A naive model that reuses one probability across sets misprices set-3 and set-5 contracts.
ten.set_number_calibration.measurement: From Sackmann score strings compute, for the favourite by edge bin, the empirical win frequency in set 1, set 2 given won/lost 1, set 3 given 1-1, bo5 set 4 and set 5 conditional on state; fit a logistic with edge, set index and prior-set result dummies, shrink toward the pooled model with n/(n+50). Output offsets in logit units per set index and state. Interpretation limit: score strings give only the net conditional offset by set index and prior-set result (latent day form, momentum and fatigue combined); separating latent form from momentum needs point-level data that exist for Slams only, as exact_set_score's es_dependence_estimation states.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings

ten.within_match_serve_decay.label: Within-match serve and movement decay profile
ten.within_match_serve_decay.mechanism: A player's serve-point win rate drifts down in later sets, and the drift differs by age, previous workload and match length.
ten.within_match_serve_decay.rationale: Late-set contracts (set 4, set 5, set 3 of a bo3) depend on fatigue effects that appear within the match rather than in rest days; a pre-match fatigue number only partly predicts it.
ten.within_match_serve_decay.measurement: From point-level or set-level serve data compute per player (spw in set k+1 minus spw in set k) averaged over bo5 matches lasting at least 3 sets; shrink toward the tour average 0.0 with n/(n+25); include age>=33, prior-match minutes>200, and heat as covariates. Report expected spw change by set index for each player.
free_sources: Sackmann slam point-by-point
